import pytest
import math

if pytest.use_correct:
    from correct_python_programs.gcd import gcd
else:
    from python_programs.gcd import gcd


def test_attack_1():
    # docstring example + classic Euclidean values
    assert gcd(35, 21) == 7
    assert gcd(48, 18) == 6
    assert gcd(1071, 462) == 21


def test_attack_2():
    # zero and one edge cases
    assert gcd(0, 5) == 5
    assert gcd(5, 0) == 5
    assert gcd(0, 1) == 1
    assert gcd(1, 0) == 1
    assert gcd(1, 1) == 1
    assert gcd(0, 0) == 0


def test_attack_3():
    # second argument larger + commutativity
    assert gcd(21, 35) == 7
    assert gcd(5, 10) == 5
    assert gcd(18, 48) == 6
    assert gcd(27, 81) == 27
    for a, b in [(35, 21), (48, 18), (1071, 462), (13, 17), (100, 80)]:
        assert gcd(a, b) == gcd(b, a)


def test_attack_4():
    # same number, coprime, divisor cases
    assert gcd(13, 13) == 13
    assert gcd(13, 17) == 1
    assert gcd(101, 103) == 1
    assert gcd(100, 80) == 20
    assert gcd(81, 27) == 27
    assert gcd(48, 180) == 12


def test_attack_5():
    # oracle comparison for non-negative inputs
    pairs = [
        (0, 5),
        (5, 0),
        (35, 21),
        (21, 35),
        (48, 18),
        (1071, 462),
        (270, 192),
        (123456, 7890),
        (13, 17),
        (100, 80),
    ]
    for a, b in pairs:
        assert gcd(a, b) == math.gcd(a, b)


def test_attack_6():
    # result divides both and is greatest
    for a, b in [(35, 21), (48, 18), (100, 80), (13, 17), (81, 27), (270, 192)]:
        g = gcd(a, b)
        assert g > 0
        assert a % g == 0
        assert b % g == 0
        for d in range(g + 1, max(a, b) + 1):
            assert not (a % d == 0 and b % d == 0)


def test_attack_7():
    # larger values and termination when a < b
    assert gcd(123456, 7890) == 6
    assert gcd(270, 192) == 6
    assert gcd(17, 31) == 1
    assert gcd(10, 5) == 5
    assert gcd(5, 10) == 5
